text.p: ON THIS DAY 23RD JUNE
** BIRTHDAYS **
The EMPRESS JOSEPHINE, the Martinique-born wife of NAPOLEON BONAPARTE whose marriage was dissolved when she failed to produce an heir, was born in 1763.
British naval captain CHAPMAN CLARE, who became the commander of the South Australian cruiser 'Protector' in the Boxer Rebellion, was born in 1853.

Japanese businessman TAIRA KASHIWAGI, who represented Thursday Island pearl-divers in Brisbane in the early 1900's, was born in 1868. Despite spending 45 years in Australia, he was still interned during World War Two.
British monarch EDWARD VIII, who abdicated in order to marry American socialite WALLIS SIMPSON, was born in 1894.
American zoologist and sociologist ALFRED KINSEY, best known for his studies of human sexual behaviour, was born in 1894.
Australian pilot KEITH VIRTUE was born in 1909.
British mathematician ALAN MATHISON TURING, who pioneered the 'Turing Machine' which greatly advanced computer equipment, was born in 1912.
British cricketer SIR LEONARD HUTTON, who scored 364 runs against Australia in 1938, was born in 1916.
American dancer, actor, director and choreographer BOB FOSSE, who won an Oscar for "Cabaret", was born in 1927.

American country and western singer JUNE CARTER was born in 1929. She began singing with her sisters in 1943, and her song "Ring Of Fire" became a big hit for her husband-to-be JOHNNY CASH (they were married in 1968). She also recorded a number of duets with him.

Australian singer DIANA TRASK, who had some television exposure in Australia before trying her luck in the United States, was born in Warburton in Victoria in 1940. Her rise to popularity in America was guided by MITCH MILLER, and she had her first hit with the 1960 song "A Guy Is A Guy".

British singer ADAM FAITH (TERRENCE NELHAMS), who began his career copying ELVIS PRESLEY, was born in 1940. He had several big hits, including "What Do You Want" (1959), "Poor Me" (1960) and "Someone Else's Baby" (1960). He later managed the career of LEO SAYER.
** EVENTS **
1810 : Australia's first Post Office was officially
opened by Governor LAUCHLAN MACQUARIE on the corner of George Street North and Circular Quay in Sydney.
The premises was owned by ISAAC NICHOLS, who became the first postmaster in the Australian colony.
1848 : ADOLPHE SAX was granted a patent for the
saxophone.
1911 : Despite gloomy and wet conditions, thousands of
people turned out to celebrate the coronation of England's KING GEORGE V in London.
1939 : The Irish Parliament suppressed the IRA (Irish
Republican Army) following a series of bombings in England.
The IRA was declared illegal in 1931, and again in 1936, but maintained its campaign against the division of Ireland.
1943 : The Minister for Labour, EDDIE WARD, claimed that
important information related to the so-called 'Brisbane Line', was missing from Australian Defence Department files.
It was claimed that during World War Two, much of Australia, north of a line drawn between Brisbane and a point north of Adelaide, would be abandoned in the event of a Japanese invasion.
1944 : The Commonwealth Food Control organisation
encouraged Australians to eat more cabbage.
1950 : The Australian Government passed a Bill, extending
child endowment to a couple's first child. The payment was 5-shillings a week!
1959 : American singer LOUIS ARMSTRONG suffered a mild
heart attack.
1964 : Three civil rights workers were reported missing
after being arrested by Mississippi Police.
Their bodies were found about 6 weeks later, and two people were arrested and charged with the murders on the 2nd of October, 1964.
The incident formed the basis of the film "Mississipii Burning" starring GENE HACKMAN.
1965 : Russia joined China and North Korea in refusing a
Commonwealth peace mission, proposed by British Prime Minister HAROLD WILSON, aimed at finding a settlement for the Vietnam war.
1976 : The parents of eight 'thalidomide children' in
three Australian States accepted a compensation offer of 700,000 dollars.
1980 : Australia's first test-tube baby, CANDICE
ELIZABETH REED, was born at the Royal Womens' Hospital in Melbourne.
1980 : British novelist OLIVIA MANNING, best known for
her Balkan Trilogy, died.
1985 : An 'Air India' jumbo jet exploded in mid-air off
the Irish coast, killing all 329 people on board.
The jet was flying from Canada, and the explosion was intially blamed on Sikh terrorists.
1991 : The International Monetary Fund agreed to offer
'associate-membership' to the Soviet Union.
